message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** (2017) – *re‑released in 2020* | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological twist on the classic horror tale, blending suspense with social commentary on abuse and gaslighting. |
| 2 | **Tenet** (2020) | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson | A mind‑bending time‑travel thriller that keeps you guessing while delivering high‑concept action sequences. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** (2020) | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen | Though more courtroom drama than pure thriller, its tense narrative and historical stakes make it a gripping watch. |
| 4 | **Uncut Gems** (2019) – *re‑released in 2020* | Ben Safdie, Joshua Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | An adrenaline‑packed heist story that showcases Sandler’s intense performance and a relentless pacing. |
| 5 | **The Hunt** (2020) | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A chilling thriller about a man falsely accused of child abuse, exploring paranoia and societal judgment. |
| 6 | **The Night House** (2020) | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Lane | A psychological horror‑thriller that blends domestic mystery with supernatural dread. |
| 7 | **The Little Things** (2020) | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek | A gritty detective story that examines obsession and moral ambiguity. |
| 8 | **The Platform** (2019) – *re‑released in 2020* | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A dystopian thriller that uses claustrophobic setting to explore class conflict and human nature. |
| 9 | **The Last Duel** (2021) – *premiered early 2020* | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver | A medieval courtroom drama that delivers tension through character dynamics and moral dilemmas. |
|10 | **The Irishman** (2019) – *re‑released in 2020* | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino | While more biographical, its slow‑burn suspense and exploration of crime history keep viewers engaged. |

> **Tip:** If you’re looking for something that leans more into the “crime” side rather than just suspense, check out *The Irishman* and *The Trial of the Chicago 7*. For pure psychological thrills, *The Invisible Man* and *The Night House* are excellent choices.

Enjoy your binge‑watch!
